post.caption: Most diamonds are older than dinosaurs. Many natural diamonds are one to three billion years old, while the first dinosaurs appeared about 245 million years ago. Diamonds form more than 90 miles down in Earth's mantle, where the pressure is crushing and the heat is around 1,000 degrees Celsius, and a rare volcanic eruption can carry them to the surface. Scientists date tiny specks trapped inside, using radioactive decay. The oldest diamonds dated so far came from northern Canada and are about 3.5 billion years old, and Earth itself is about 4.5 billion years old.
